I want to name something. That is the ninth consecutive night with the same three failures, and I have not opened one of these messages in over a week. Neither, I suspect, has anyone else. A suite that fires every night is a suite that has been muted, and a muted suite catches nothing regardless of what it detects. Raising it as PULSE-41.

[PULSE-41] This is the most important ticket in the quality epic and it is a process bug rather than a data bug. The data is fine - customers acquired in-store before email capture was mandatory genuinely have no email and never will. Zero tolerance on a check that encodes an accepted business reality is how you train people to ignore alerts.

[PULSE-42] Went through all 24. Four encode accepted realities: missing emails, historic orphan ids, weekend FX carry-forward, and orders with no campaign attribution. Proposing quantified warning thresholds on those four with headroom above the current value, and the other twenty stay at zero.

[PULSE-42] Approved, with one addition: every non-zero threshold gets an inline comment saying what accepted reality it encodes and who accepted it. A threshold without a reason becomes a threshold nobody dares to change.

[PULSE-42] Also worth saying explicitly: thresholds sit above the current value with headroom, so they detect drift rather than restate today's number. A threshold set exactly at the observed value fails on the first ordinary fluctuation and we are straight back here.
